title: Keep every tied optimum
description: Distinct candidates can share the best feasible score.
oracle: Hand enumeration: truth scores A=1, B=1, C=4, D=6. A and B tie for the minimum; inclusive lower-bound comparison retains B.

title: An optimum with uncertain feasibility
description: A retained candidate can be better than the certified incumbent without certified feasibility.
oracle: Hand enumeration: all three true slacks are -1 and true scores are 4, 0, 7. The uncertain-feasibility candidate is the unique optimum.

title: No certified incumbent
description: When all remaining feasibility intervals cross zero, screening must preserve all possibilities.
oracle: Hand enumeration: only A and C are feasible; their scores are 1 and 7. No constraint upper bound is nonpositive among possible candidates.

title: An infeasible finite universe
description: Every candidate violates at least one independently checked constraint.
oracle: Hand enumeration: A violates c1, B violates c2, C violates both. This proves infeasibility of these three candidates only.

title: A tight nonzero regret bound
description: The best certified upper bound need not belong to the truly best candidate.
oracle: Hand solution: min true score is B=0, incumbent A=2; actual regret 2 equals the conditional bound 2-0.

title: Exhaustive integer design problem
description: A constrained quadratic design objective is evaluated on an 81-candidate integer grid.
oracle: Independent enumeration: x,y in {0,...,8}; f=(x-3)^2+2(y-5)^2, g1=x+y-9, g2=2-x. Nonnegative f has unique zero (3,5), which satisfies both constraints. Formula truth is recomputed independently at runtime.

title: Signed objectives and combined constraints
description: A signed linear objective is screened under the maximum of two constraint slacks.
oracle: Independent enumeration: a,b in {0,2,4}; f=2a-3b+1/2, g=max(a+b-6,1-a). Feasible points: (2,0),(2,2),(2,4),(4,0),(4,2). Minimum is -15/2 at (2,4). Score intervals propagate a,b uncertainty +/-1/10 through signed coefficients; combined slack uncertainty is +/-1/10. Formula truth recomputed at runtime.

title: Maximization as a normalized objective
description: A benefit is negated to minimize it under an exact budget constraint.
oracle: Hand enumeration: budget=3 excludes C (cost 4, benefit 13). Among feasible benefits 5,7,11,2, D has maximum 11; negation gives minimum -11.

title: An order smaller than float precision
description: Exact rational scores distinguish candidates that collapse to the same binary float.
oracle: Hand solution: A=1/3; B=A+1/(3*10^30)>A; C=A+1>A. No rounding or tolerance is part of the comparison.

title: Loose intervals
description: The same six true candidates are screened with intentionally uninformative intervals.
oracle: Hand enumeration: true scores A..F are 0,2,4,6,8,10. The refined case uses [s-1/4,s+1/4] inside each loose [-1,12] interval. Both worlds share the same candidate IDs and truth.

title: Tightened intervals
description: The same six true candidates are screened with narrower intervals.
oracle: Hand enumeration: true scores A..F are 0,2,4,6,8,10. The refined case uses [s-1/4,s+1/4] inside each loose [-1,12] interval. Both worlds share the same candidate IDs and truth.

title: Negative control: false score interval
description: A deliberately incorrect interval can screen out the true optimum.
oracle: Hand solution: B=0<A=1, but B is falsely declared to lie in [2,2]. The true optimum is discarded and claimed conditional regret bound fails; replay must expose the invalid premise.

title: Negative control: false infeasibility
description: A deliberately incorrect constraint interval can falsely reject the best candidate.
oracle: Hand solution: both true constraints are -1, so B=0 is feasible and better than A=1. The false [1,1] constraint interval rejects B. Replay must expose the unsound constraint premise.
